args.message: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

args.body:
## Summary
`round_money` in `src/money.py` was using `ROUND_HALF_UP`, which caused the nightly build to fail since `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212.

## Changes
- Replaced `ROUND_HALF_UP` with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `src/money.py`.

## Verification
- CI run `ci-0001` on branch `fix-bankers-rounding` (sha 08d3cd5986) passed, including `tests/test_money.py`.

Reviewer: @alex (code owner approval required to merge into main).

transcript.content: The bug is clear: `round_money` uses `ROUND_HALF_UP` instead of `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. Let me create a branch and fix it.
transcript.reasoning_content:
Note: 2.675 as Decimal literal quantize with ROUND_HALF_EVEN gives 2.68 (since Decimal is exact, 2.675 -> half, even digit: 7 is odd -> rounds up to 2.68). 2.665 -> 2.66 (6 even, stays). Good.

Create branch, commit fix, run CI.

function.name: commit_changes

transcript.content: The fix aligns with the test expectations: `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` on exact Decimals gives 2.675 → 2.68 (rounds to even 8) and 2.665 → 2.66 (rounds to even 6). Now let me run CI.
transcript.reasoning_content: Note: test expects 2.675 → 2.68. With ROUND_HALF_EVEN on Decimal("2.675"), quantize to 0.01... Decimal("2.675") is exact, so ROUND_HALF_EVEN would give 2.68 (since 2.67 vs 2.68, tie → even digit: 7 is odd, 8 is even → 2.68). And 2.665 → tie → 2.66 (6 even). Yes both pass with ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Good.

transcript.content: CI passed. Now I'll open the PR against main with alex as the reviewer.
